summary: Layer Promotion Error is plausibly distinct if framed as monotonic evidence-layer checking for cultural/artifact research pipelines, not generic fact-checking. Strongest collision risk is claim verification, provenance validation, SHACL/type checking, and hallucination detection.
blocking_issues: Missing prior-art clusters: FEVER/SciFact/AVeriTeC, attribution/factuality, SHACL/ShEx, information-flow type systems, digital humanities source criticism, cultural heritage uncertainty, CARE/Local Contexts, benchmark validity.

summary: The 30-case benchmark is meaningful only as a seeded construct test. Perfect precision/recall is weak evidence because data and detector are co-designed, labels leak through metadata, lexical cues are hand-picked, and there is no blind annotation or held-out set.
blocking_issues: Needs 300-500 independent claims, blind annotation, agreement metrics, locked splits, baselines, hard negatives, uncertainty, robustness checks, metadata-free scoring.

summary: A top venue would reject this today as an internal sanity check. It becomes nontrivial only when it detects layer-promotion failures in real, previously unseen artifact-derived outputs and beats credible baselines.
blocking_issues: Needs 100+ cases with at least 30% external/cross-project, baselines, inter-annotator agreement, prior-art proof, domain and rights review, and evidence that at least one plausible false publication claim is prevented.
